title: Recover a boot-looping API service
scenario: A systemd unit repeatedly starts before its generated environment file exists and hits the start limit after reboot. Preserve its sandboxing and make startup deterministic.
success: After two cold boots the API is healthy within 30 seconds; ordering is explicit; restart storms stop; hardening properties are unchanged.

title: Explain a memory kill with free RAM
scenario: A Java worker is killed every afternoon although host metrics show free memory. Find the controlling limit and leave a concise evidence-backed diagnosis without raising it.
success: The report identifies the exact cgroup and OOM evidence; includes the effective limit and peak; changes no runtime state; a hidden sibling cgroup is not blamed.

title: Restore uploads without disabling SELinux
scenario: A new mounted upload volume returns permission denied only through the web service. DAC permissions look correct and an operator suggests setenforce 0.
success: Uploads and reads work after reboot; the mount has a persistent correct label; enforcing mode remains enabled; unrelated labels are unchanged.

environment: Linux VM with LVM and ext4
title: Extend a full filesystem online
scenario: The application volume is full while its volume group has free extents. The service cannot be stopped and a second similarly named volume must not be touched.
success: The intended filesystem and LV grow by the requested amount online; existing checksums match; the sibling LV is unchanged; the service remains available.

title: Replace a failed RAID member safely
scenario: One synthetic disk in a degraded RAID10 has failed and its replacement contains a stale signature. Restore redundancy without losing writes made during rebuild.
success: The array becomes clean with the replacement member; canary writes survive; stale metadata is removed only from the replacement; boot assembly remains valid.

title: Fix log rotation that fills root
scenario: A chatty daemon writes a large log because rotation silently fails after a package migration. Configure bounded retention without interrupting the daemon.
success: Forced and scheduled rotations succeed; the daemon reopens its log; retention and compression match policy; root usage stabilizes; no log gap exceeds tolerance.

title: Create a reproducible internal package
scenario: A shell-installed utility must become a signed Debian package with configuration preserved across upgrades and a pinned dependency.
success: Two builds produce equivalent package payloads; signature verifies; install and upgrade pass; edited config survives upgrade; dependency is exact.

title: Remove a NUMA latency regression
scenario: A pinned packet-processing service lost throughput after a CPU topology change. Diagnose affinity and memory placement while retaining its CPU budget.
success: P99 falls below the threshold under replay; CPU quota is unchanged; placement matches the active NIC NUMA node; restart preserves the setting.

environment: Linux VM with cron and systemd timers
title: Make a backup schedule timezone-safe
scenario: A legacy cron job runs twice during daylight-saving fallback and overlaps with itself. Replace it with an observable non-overlapping schedule.
success: Exactly one run occurs for the simulated date; concurrent execution is prevented; missed-run behavior is defined; logs expose success and failure.

title: Contain a fork and file-descriptor storm
scenario: A service intermittently spawns children and leaks sockets until the host becomes unstable. Stabilize it and capture enough evidence for later debugging.
success: The host remains responsive under recurrence; the service has justified process and FD limits; evidence identifies the spawning path; healthy throughput stays above target.

title: Restore asymmetric routing
scenario: A dual-homed service accepts requests on one interface but replies through the other and is dropped upstream. Repair policy routing without changing the default route for maintenance traffic.
success: Connections through both ingress paths complete; replies use their ingress uplink; maintenance traffic retains its route; rules persist after namespace restart.

title: Find intermittent DNS SERVFAIL
scenario: Only large signed DNS answers fail through one resolver path. Packet captures and resolver metrics are available among noisy logs.
success: The diagnosis proves the transport and size-related cause; identifies the failing hop; proposes a bounded fix; makes no speculative production change.

title: Perform a safe DNSSEC key rollover
scenario: A zone has a prepublished successor key but automation stalled before rollover. Complete the sequence without producing an unsigned or bogus validation window.
success: The zone validates throughout simulated resolver polling; old and new signatures overlap correctly; serials increase; obsolete private material is retired safely.

title: Repair an incomplete TLS chain
scenario: Browsers with an empty intermediate cache reject one virtual host while local curl succeeds. Fix the served chain without changing its leaf key.
success: Independent TLS validation succeeds with only the root trusted; leaf fingerprint is unchanged; chain order is correct; OCSP stapling remains healthy.

title: Configure resilient weighted load balancing
scenario: Two stable backends and one canary need weighted traffic with active health checks and connection draining during removal.
success: Observed distribution matches tolerance; failed nodes receive no new requests; in-flight requests drain; recovery reintroduces capacity; admin endpoints are private.

title: Stop a route leak with policy
scenario: A new peer receives internal prefixes and advertises an accidental default. Correct import and export policy while preserving approved customer routes.
success: Forbidden prefixes never cross the boundary; the accidental default is rejected; approved routes converge; max-prefix and explicit deny safeguards exist.

title: Add a least-route site VPN
scenario: Connect two overlapping private networks for one application subnet through translated addresses. Do not route general Internet traffic through the tunnel.
success: Only declared application flows cross the encrypted tunnel; overlap translation is stable; Internet routes stay local; restart restores peers and rules.

title: Fix HTTP/2 gRPC retries safely
scenario: Transient upstream resets break reads while naive retries duplicate writes. Configure protocol-aware retry and timeout behavior for the two RPC classes.
success: Idempotent reads recover within budget; writes execute at most once; gRPC status mapping is correct; retry storms are capped; metrics distinguish outcomes.

title: Isolate tenants without breaking DHCP
scenario: Two tenant bridges can reach each other after an iptables-to-nftables migration. Restore isolation while keeping DHCP DNS and outbound NAT.
success: Cross-tenant probes fail; allowed infrastructure and egress flows pass; established connections behave as specified; one atomic persistent ruleset owns policy.

environment: Anycast service with FRR and HAProxy
title: Drain an unhealthy anycast site
scenario: One site returns corrupt responses but its routing session is healthy. Withdraw traffic based on application health without causing route flaps or overloading the other site.
success: Bad responses cease within the objective; withdrawal is damped; the healthy site remains below capacity; recovery requires a stable health window; timeline is recorded.

title: Make a container survive read-only root
scenario: A service must run with a read-only root filesystem but currently writes cache PID and temporary files into image paths.
success: The service passes tests with read-only root; only declared tmpfs or volumes are writable; it runs non-root; restart preserves only intended state.

title: Shrink and accelerate a Go image build
scenario: A 1.4 GB Go image includes compilers source and credentials and invalidates dependencies on every edit.
success: The runtime image is below the limit; no build secret or compiler remains; dependency caching works; binary and CA behavior pass on two architectures.

title: Publish a deterministic multi-architecture image
scenario: Build amd64 and arm64 variants from one source with matching labels and an OCI index while avoiding emulation for tests that can run natively.
success: Both variants pass native smoke tests; index resolves correctly; provenance names the same source commit; rebuild manifests are reproducible within defined fields.

title: Repair startup and graceful shutdown
scenario: A Compose stack relies on start order instead of readiness and loses queued jobs when stopped. Correct health gating and termination semantics.
success: Cold start succeeds under delayed database readiness; shutdown drains accepted jobs inside the grace period; no fixed sleeps are used; restart policy avoids loops.

title: Investigate a container escape alert
scenario: A canary container touched a host-visible path. Determine the misconfiguration and contain it while preserving forensic artifacts.
success: The exploit path is blocked; evidence hashes and timeline are retained; unrelated workloads continue; privileged and mount capabilities are minimized; canary replay fails.

title: Audit an image for secret and license risk
scenario: An image proposed for release has layered filesystem history an SBOM and package metadata. Produce a release decision and remediation list.
success: The report finds secrets including deleted-layer content; identifies policy-disallowed licenses and critical packages; contains no secret values; gives verifiable locations.

title: Migrate a privileged service to rootless
scenario: A system container binds a low port and writes a named volume as root. Move it to a user service without changing its public endpoint or data ownership semantics.
success: The endpoint and data survive reboot; no root daemon or privileged container is used; subordinate IDs are correct; backup tooling can still read consistent snapshots.

title: Enforce signed image promotion
scenario: Only CI-built images from the release workflow may enter the production repository. Tags are mutable and developer keys must not be trusted.
success: Valid keyless attestations promote by digest; unsigned replayed or wrong-workflow images fail; production references are immutable; decisions are auditable.

title: Recover registry garbage collection
scenario: An interrupted garbage collection left orphan blobs and one manifest temporarily unreadable. Restore consistency and reclaim only unreachable content.
success: All referenced manifests and layers pull with original digests; orphan bytes are reclaimed; uploads resume; a second GC is safe; recovery steps are documented.

title: Stop GPU workload interference
scenario: Two inference containers contend for GPUs because device exposure and runtime classes drifted. Isolate allocations and retain health during rolling replacement.
success: Each workload sees only assigned devices; utilization and latency meet limits; runtime configuration survives restart; a rolling update never double-allocates a device.

title: Repair a CrashLooping web deployment
scenario: A deployment fails after a ConfigMap key rename and its liveness probe masks the original error. Restore service without weakening health checks.
success: All replicas become ready; correct configuration is mounted; probes reflect actual health; rollout history is useful; unrelated ConfigMap keys remain intact.

title: Restore DNS under default deny
scenario: A namespace default-deny rollout isolated workloads as intended but also broke name resolution and one required outbound API.
success: Pods resolve cluster names and reach only the approved API; arbitrary egress and peer namespaces remain blocked; policy selects intended pods only.

title: Move an API between namespaces with no downtime
scenario: Migrate a live API and its configuration to a new namespace while retaining its hostname and in-flight requests.
success: Continuous probes show no failed requests; old and new endpoints never serve conflicting versions; secrets are not copied unnecessarily; old resources are retired.

title: Autoscale on a workload signal
scenario: CPU is flat while queue age grows. Configure metrics and autoscaling that reacts to oldest-job age without oscillating at idle.
success: Replicas scale before the latency SLO is breached; drain back gradually; metrics failures do not collapse capacity; min max and stabilization are explicit.

title: Recover a stuck stateful volume attachment
scenario: A rescheduled database pod is blocked by a stale attachment after simulated node loss. Recover it without simultaneous mounts or deleting the volume.
success: Exactly one node mounts the volume; database checksums pass; stale attachment clears through supported APIs; recurrence has a documented safe runbook.

title: Enforce workload security with exceptions
scenario: Apply restricted workload defaults while allowing a narrowly scoped legacy daemon exception that expires automatically.
success: Noncompliant new pods are denied with useful messages; compliant pods run; exception matches only named workload fields and expires; existing inventory is reported.

title: Fix requests that strand capacity
scenario: Poor requests and topology constraints leave nodes half empty while replicas stay pending. Improve placement without violating zone redundancy.
success: All required replicas schedule; zone skew stays within one; peak node pressure stays safe under load; requests reflect measured usage; eviction rate does not rise.

title: Recover an expired control-plane certificate
scenario: The API is unavailable after certificate expiry but etcd data is intact. Restore control plane access and establish monitored renewal.
success: Cluster objects and etcd revision are preserved; all control-plane components are healthy; kubeconfigs work; renewed certificates have intended lifetimes and alerts.

title: Upgrade manifests across an API removal
scenario: A cluster upgrade is blocked by removed workload and policy APIs plus one custom webhook that rejects the new shape.
success: Stored and declared resources use supported APIs; semantic policy behavior is preserved; upgrade simulation passes; rollback artifacts and conversion evidence exist.

title: Stabilize a cascading node-pressure incident
scenario: A zone loss triggers rescheduling then disk and connection pressure elsewhere. Restore the critical service while protecting quorum workloads and preventing repeated eviction.
success: Critical SLO recovers; quorum never falls below safety; eviction loop stops; lower priority work yields capacity; changes include clear rollback and incident timeline.

title: Import an unmanaged resource safely
scenario: A manually created object must enter state without replacement and then receive two policy tags.
success: Plan after import contains only intended in-place tag changes; object identity and data remain; second plan is empty; import address is documented.

title: Remove unstable for_each addressing
scenario: A module indexes subnets by list position so inserting one subnet proposes widespread replacement. Migrate to stable keys without recreating existing resources.
success: State migration produces no replacement for existing subnets; the new subnet is additive; reorder is a no-op; outputs retain compatible types.

title: Recover from a stale state lock
scenario: A killed pipeline left a lock while another operator may still be active. Determine ownership and recover safely without corrupting state.
success: Only a provably stale lock is removed; concurrent-live simulation is refused; state serial and lineage remain valid; plan converges; actions are recorded.

title: Create an idempotent rolling role
scenario: Build a role that updates a proxy one node at a time validates configuration and rolls back a bad template.
success: Second run reports no changes; at least two nodes stay healthy; invalid configuration never activates; rollback restores checksum; handlers run only when needed.

title: Build and verify a hardened base image
scenario: Produce a reproducible VM image with CIS-inspired controls cloud-init and an auditable package manifest while retaining emergency console access.
success: Image boots in clean VM; controls and console tests pass; no machine identity or credential is baked in; manifest and source revision are embedded.

title: Block a risky infrastructure plan
scenario: Review a large plan containing a subtle database replacement public exposure and IAM wildcard among harmless churn. Implement policy checks.
success: Policy denies all three risks with resource-level messages; accepts provided safe plan; ignores order-only noise; supports an explicit time-bounded exception record.

title: Upgrade a provider with schema changes
scenario: Move a pinned provider across a breaking major version that changes defaults and deprecates nested blocks without changing deployed behavior.
success: Lockfile pins checksums; state upgrades; plan is empty against existing infrastructure; apply on a fresh stack matches; compatibility notes identify intentional changes.

environment: Synthetic cloud billing API and Terraform
title: Reduce idle cloud cost without hurting recovery
scenario: Inventory a staging estate with unattached storage oversized instances and snapshot retention requirements. Implement safe savings.
success: Monthly modeled cost falls by target; protected and recent recovery assets remain; utilization SLO passes; schedules are timezone-safe; every deletion candidate has evidence.

title: Publish a self-service database composite
scenario: Create a portable database claim with size classes encrypted storage connection secrets and deletion protection.
success: Valid claims become ready; invalid sizes fail early; secrets are namespace-scoped; composition updates do not replace instances; deletion policy retains production data.

title: Revoke a compromised deployment role
scenario: A CI role token was exposed across three accounts. Contain access rotate trust and prove infrastructure reconciliation still works.
success: Old token and derived sessions lose access within objective; least-privilege replacement deploys; unrelated roles remain; audit query enumerates attempted use and changes.

title: Fix cache poisoning across pull requests
scenario: An untrusted pull request can populate a dependency cache later restored by protected release jobs. Redesign cache scope and permissions.
success: Untrusted content cannot influence release artifacts; trusted cache hits still occur; fork jobs have read-only minimum permissions; attack fixture is rejected.

title: Build a selective monorepo pipeline
scenario: A monorepo rebuilds every service on every commit. Create dependency-aware jobs while ensuring shared-library changes fan out correctly.
success: Changed services and all reverse dependencies test; unrelated services skip; merge-base edge cases work; generated pipeline is deterministic; full scheduled build remains.

title: Make deployment retries safe
scenario: A pipeline retry after timeout can deploy twice and overwrite the recorded release. Make stages resumable and idempotent.
success: Repeated or resumed runs produce one deployment per version; locks are scoped; completed stages are not repeated unsafely; final record matches live digest.

title: Attach verifiable build provenance
scenario: A build produces an image but consumers cannot prove source workflow or builder identity. Add signed SLSA-style provenance.
success: Attestation binds source revision builder parameters and image digest; verification passes offline; altered artifact or provenance fails; signing secret is not exposed.

title: Implement an automated canary release
scenario: Release a service through 5 25 and 50 percent stages using latency and error signals with automatic abort.
success: Healthy release promotes; injected regression aborts before broad exposure; stable ReplicaSet remains available; analysis handles missing metrics conservatively.

title: Eliminate a timestamp-only rebuild
scenario: A generated artifact changes every run due only to embedded wall-clock time and breaks reproducibility and caching.
success: Clean builds in separate paths have identical hashes; version metadata remains meaningful; incremental build skips unchanged work; dirty-source behavior is defined.

title: Split a release train without breaking consumers
scenario: One library needs an emergency major release while the rest of the train stays compatible. Adjust versioning changelogs and publishing order.
success: Dependency constraints resolve for old and new consumers; tags and artifacts correspond; changelog identifies breaking change; rerunning publish cannot overwrite versions.

title: Repair flaky integration test orchestration
scenario: Parallel tests collide on ports databases and cleanup causing nondeterministic failures. Isolate resources without serializing the suite.
success: Repeated stress runs pass; workers have unique resources; cleanup occurs on failure and cancellation; runtime remains within budget; failures retain diagnostics.

title: Reconstruct a deleted release artifact
scenario: A release blob was deleted but signed build outputs and checksums remain in isolated runners. Recover without inventing a new artifact under the old version.
success: Recovered bytes match signed digest; provenance verifies; metadata records recovery; any rebuild mismatch is refused; consumers can fetch through normal endpoint.

title: Halt and unwind a bad global release
scenario: A release is healthy in canary but corrupts region-specific data elsewhere. Stop propagation and roll back safely despite an incompatible schema step.
success: No additional regions promote; affected traffic uses compatible code and schema; data repair is idempotent; healthy regions remain; release state reflects reality.

title: Fix a cardinality explosion
scenario: A request metric labels every user and URL causing Prometheus memory growth. Preserve useful service and route visibility with bounded cardinality.
success: Series count remains below limit under randomized traffic; status method and normalized route queries work; user identity is absent; recording rules still evaluate.

title: Connect one request across signals
scenario: Instrument and route an API so a trace ID connects structured logs traces and an exemplar-bearing latency metric.
success: A synthetic request is discoverable in all three backends by trace ID; context crosses one async hop; sampling keeps errors; secrets and bodies are excluded.

title: Correct a misleading availability dashboard
scenario: A dashboard averages per-instance ratios and reports green during a large-instance outage. Replace it with traffic-weighted queries and defined no-traffic behavior.
success: Panels match fixture ground truth; aggregate numerator and denominator correctly; no-traffic renders as specified; labels and units are consistent; hidden replica mix passes.

title: Create actionable multiwindow SLO alerts
scenario: Build fast-burn and slow-burn alerts for a 99.9 percent API SLO with maintenance inhibition and ownership routing.
success: Synthetic burn patterns page or ticket at intended windows; brief noise does not page; maintenance inhibits only scoped service; alerts link runbook and expose budget impact.

title: Restore multiline exception ingestion
scenario: Stack traces are split into unrelated log entries and labels contain request IDs. Repair parsing and labeling without losing source timestamps.
success: Each exception is one ordered event; request ID is parsed data not a label; timestamps match source; malformed lines remain discoverable; cardinality stays bounded.

title: Find a tail-latency dependency
scenario: Median latency is flat but P99 doubled after a release. Use traces to identify a conditional fan-out and provide evidence rather than changing code.
success: Report identifies trigger span and downstream dependency; quantifies affected cohort and critical path; rules out supplied decoys; links reproducible queries.

title: Make an external probe test the user path
scenario: A probe checks an origin IP over HTTP and stays green through DNS and certificate failures. Redesign it to cover the public HTTPS path.
success: Probe validates DNS TCP TLS hostname and expected content; failures identify phase; origin-only success cannot pass; probe credentials are protected.

title: Triage an error-budget burn
scenario: Checkout errors spike amid simultaneous deploy database and network signals. Identify the cause mitigate it and maintain an incident timeline.
success: Error rate returns below threshold; mitigation addresses causal signal; unrelated rollback is avoided; timeline uses telemetry timestamps; follow-up query detects recurrence.

title: Reduce metrics cost while preserving investigations
scenario: Long-term metrics storage exceeds budget due to raw high-frequency blocks. Configure compaction retention and downsampling for stated forensic queries.
success: Modeled storage falls by target; recent raw and long-range aggregate queries meet resolution contracts; deletion delay protects partial uploads; compactor is singleton.

title: Restore monitoring during a control-plane outage
scenario: Central monitoring and its identity provider are unavailable during an incident. Establish a bounded break-glass view without weakening normal authentication permanently.
success: On-call can access required read-only signals; access is time-limited audited and isolated; normal auth resumes automatically; no write or tenant-crossing capability is exposed.

title: Harden SSH without locking out automation
scenario: Remove password and root login while a deployment account still needs noninteractive access through a restricted key.
success: Approved key deploys required files; password root forwarding and unrelated commands fail; host key continuity holds; config validation precedes reload.

title: Issue short-lived database credentials
scenario: Replace a shared static database password with per-job dynamic credentials and automatic revocation.
success: Jobs receive unique least-privilege credentials; TTL and renewal match duration; cancellation revokes promptly; root credential is not exposed; audit entries identify jobs.

title: Repair a broken identity rotation
scenario: Workloads fail mutual TLS after an intermediate rotation because one trust bundle and one clock are stale. Restore service safely.
success: All intended identities authenticate; stale or wrong-selector identities fail; bundles overlap through rotation; clock correction is bounded; no certificate lifetime is extended.

title: Codify infrastructure guardrails
scenario: Implement policies requiring encryption ownership and private access while allowing documented development exceptions.
success: Unsafe fixtures fail with precise messages; safe fixtures pass; exceptions require owner expiry and scope; expired or wildcard exceptions fail closed.

title: Contain cryptomining in a workload
scenario: A compromised pod launches a miner and probes the cluster API. Contain it preserve evidence and close the initial permissions gap.
success: Malicious traffic and process stop; image filesystem and audit evidence are hashed; service recovers from trusted digest; service account loses excess rights; replay is detected.

title: Purge and rotate a leaked canary secret
scenario: A canary credential appears in current files and earlier commits. Remove exposure and produce a coordinated rotation plan without displaying its value.
success: Scanners find no credential in reachable history; old credential is revoked in emulator; replacement reaches intended consumer securely; commit mapping and collaborator action are documented.

title: Require deployable artifact attestations
scenario: Production requires signed images an SBOM vulnerability policy and a matching source repository attestation.
success: Compliant digest deploys; mutable tag signature wrong repository stale scan and high-severity fixture fail; verifier outage follows declared fail-safe policy.

title: Restore useful privileged-action auditing
scenario: An overbroad audit configuration drops events under load and floods disk with harmless reads. Tune it for specified privileged changes.
success: All target actions are recorded with actor path and outcome under stress; irrelevant rate is bounded; loss counter stays zero; rules persist and are immutable after boot.

title: Rotate a root CA with constrained overlap
scenario: Move services to a new root across staggered clients while preventing newly issued certificates under the old hierarchy.
success: Connectivity holds through staged overlap; new issuance chains only to new root; old clients age out by deadline; final trust excludes old root; rollback boundary is explicit.

title: Investigate impossible-travel admin access
scenario: Two admin sessions appear continents apart amid proxy logs token records and clock skew. Decide whether compromise occurred and contain proportionately.
success: Conclusion reconciles trusted timestamps and proxy chain; compromised tokens are revoked if supported; unaffected access is preserved; evidence chain and detection improvement are recorded.

title: Restore an accidentally dropped table
scenario: A table was dropped after the last full backup while WAL archiving is healthy. Recover it to immediately before the drop without rewinding other tables.
success: Recovered table matches pre-drop checksum and row count; post-drop changes to other tables remain; recovery target is evidenced; production instance was not destructively rewound.

title: Fix replication lag caused by a slot
scenario: A replica falls behind while a logical slot also retains WAL until disk pressure rises. Restore headroom without losing the required subscriber position.
success: Replica catches up; disk stays below threshold; required slot continuity holds or is safely reestablished; alerts cover lag bytes time and retained WAL.

title: Perform a zero-downtime column migration
scenario: Replace a heavily used text identifier with UUID semantics across old and new application versions.
success: Mixed versions read and write throughout; backfill is resumable and bounded; constraints validate; final schema has one source of truth; rollback works before cutover.

title: Fix a query without hiding writes
scenario: A reporting query causes latency spikes. Add or alter indexing based on evidence without disabling durability or globally increasing resources.
success: P95 meets target on representative data; result set matches; write overhead stays below budget; chosen plan is stable; durability variables are unchanged.

title: Recover from a partial failover
scenario: A network partition promoted a replica while an old primary accepted isolated writes. Reconcile service and account for divergent synthetic records.
success: One authoritative primary remains; acknowledged safe-side writes persist; divergent records are enumerated and handled per policy; clients refresh topology; recurrence test passes.

title: Stop poison-message partition starvation
scenario: One malformed event causes a consumer to crash repeatedly and prevents later records in that partition. Add bounded retries and a dead-letter path.
success: Valid later events process in order allowed by contract; poison event retains payload metadata and reason safely; retries are bounded; replay tooling prevents duplicates.

title: Move mirrored queues to quorum queues
scenario: Migrate durable queues with publishers and consumers active while preserving confirms TTL dead-lettering and ordering constraints.
success: No acknowledged message is lost; duplicates stay within declared contract; policies match semantics; nodes may restart safely; old queues and policies are removed after validation.

title: Create encrypted verifiable backups
scenario: Back up application files and a consistent database dump with retention and unattended integrity checks.
success: Restore to an empty host reproduces checksums and database state; repository is encrypted; credentials are excluded from snapshots; retention and check jobs are idempotent.

title: Recover from simulated ransomware deletion
scenario: An attacker deleted current objects and planted encrypted replacements while versioning remained enabled. Restore the last clean point at scale.
success: Clean versions and metadata return; malicious and post-cutoff objects are handled per policy; operation is resumable; inventory proves counts and hashes; attacker token is revoked.

title: Protect quorum during a regional partition
scenario: Latency and packet loss split a five-node database across regions while clients keep retrying. Preserve consistency and restore bounded availability.
success: No split-brain writes commit; quorum side serves within SLO; minority is fenced; client retries are bounded; rejoin converges without data loss; decision timeline is recorded.

title: Onboard a service with ownership metadata
scenario: Add an existing service to the catalog with owner lifecycle dependencies docs and operational links that remain valid after repository moves.
success: Catalog validation passes; ownership resolves to a real group; dependency graph is correct; links use stable references; scorecard detects missing runbook fixture.

title: Create a promotion path without config drift
scenario: Promote one immutable artifact from development to staging to production while environments retain intentional differences.
success: Same digest advances by reviewed commits; overlays contain only declared differences; direct live mutation self-heals and alerts; rollback is a single auditable revert.

title: Provision a guarded team namespace
scenario: Offer self-service namespace creation with quota network isolation workload policy RBAC and cost labels.
success: A valid request converges completely; team admin cannot escape namespace or raise quota; cross-tenant traffic fails; platform controllers retain access; deletion handles finalizers.

title: Allocate shared platform cost fairly
scenario: Build a reproducible allocation for compute idle capacity observability and egress across teams with missing and late labels.
success: Every cost dollar is allocated or explicitly unallocated; rules are deterministic; totals reconcile; missing-label policy is visible; team output avoids cross-tenant detail.

title: Evolve a golden path without breaking adopters
scenario: A service template needs a new deployment model while dozens of generated repositories still use the old contract.
success: New projects use v2; old projects validate and upgrade through an automated path; generated diffs preserve local edits; version and deprecation telemetry are available.

title: Stop two reconcilers fighting
scenario: A Helm release operator and GitOps controller repeatedly overwrite the same fields. Establish one clear ownership model.
success: Reconciliation reaches stable zero diff; chosen owner applies intended change; rollback works; no global ignore masks unrelated drift; ownership is documented in code.

title: Fail service traffic to another cluster
scenario: One cluster loses its data plane while global discovery remains stale. Shift only stateless traffic and preserve identity policy.
success: Eligible requests fail over within objective; stateful service stays fenced; mutual identity checks hold; stale endpoints receive no traffic; failback is gradual and observable.

title: Turn a vague runbook into an executable one
scenario: A critical-service runbook says restart and check logs but omits access validation rollback and success criteria. Make it usable in a simulation.
success: A cold operator completes simulation within time; commands are safe and scoped; prerequisites decision points rollback and verification are explicit; links pass checks.

title: Implement pull-request environments with budgets
scenario: Create preview environments that handle concurrent updates DNS TLS seeded data and automatic cleanup without exposing production secrets.
success: Each PR gets isolated reachable environment; updates converge; close and TTL delete all billable resources; quotas cap abuse; only synthetic scoped secrets are present.

environment: Game-day environment across Kubernetes DNS and database
title: Recover a regional service under compound failure
scenario: A certificate expires during regional failover while database promotion automation stalls and DNS caches an unhealthy endpoint. Lead recovery under an explicit data-loss bound.
success: Service returns within objectives; committed data loss stays within bound; certificate identity and database role are correct; DNS converges safely; full timeline and follow-ups reconcile actions.
